text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonian government passes law on ombudsman who is expected to protect citizens whose rights were infringed by the regime's system and institutions.
- The Socialist party decided to remain in government coalition at its central committee session on Thursday.

- PDP ethnic Aolbanian party's dilemma over whether or not to stay in the government opens up an issue of whether Albanian political parties should continue their activities within the Macedonian system or not, paper comments.

- Albanian party representatives in parliament opposed to the govenment draft law to channel $11.16 million of IMF funds for development of east and south Macedonia (Ethnic Albanians in Macedonia are mainly concentrated in western parts).
- Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro to visit Skopje on February 26 at the invitation of President Kiro Gligorov.

- The situation in Macedonia is identical to or even worse than that in Serbia and Bulgaria but thanks to the opposition's constructive approach there are no massive protests in the streets, the leader of Macedonia's largest opposition party IMPRO-DPMNY, Ljupco Georgievski, said he had explained during his visit to the U.S.
- Owners of Jugomarket and Alfa S banks, Jasmin Moralic and Slobodan Tosevski, were arrested Thursday over the disappearance of funds equivalent to over 30 million German marks.
